findings.reason: a worker on §7 under an exact spec either blocks on the absent shared fetch or quietly duplicates it, and the drift between two copies of one fetch is the defect this plan exists to prevent.
findings.text: §7's Deliverable says the reflex acceptance tests commits "against the remote primary ref, through the same helper and fetch §5 uses", but §5 (line 60) runs `git fetch origin <primary>` inline in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` and names no shared fetch function; §7's write paths are `reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py` and the new test, and §5's are `reckon/crew/promotion.py` and `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, so no declared write path can hold the shared fetch both sections claim to use, and §7's gate is also unmet as written

findings.reason: one of the two refusal causes the deliverable promises is measured by nothing, so the section can be closed with that branch unimplemented.
findings.text: §5's Deliverable refuses when "the helper answers no remote-tracking ref" (the empty answer at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:988`, where a tree with no remote-tracking ref returns `""`), but every refusal arm in the done-when uses an unmerged head, a fast-forwarded-but-unpushed head or an unreachable remote, so an implementation that reads the empty answer as "cannot decide, promote" passes the whole gate

findings.reason: the arm set cannot fail on the branch the deliverable names, so §7 could land having implemented only the fetch-failure half and read as complete.
findings.text: §7's Deliverable names the same two causes ("when the fetch fails or the ref is missing"), but its done-when has one declining arm (unreachable remote) and none in which the remote is reachable and carries no primary ref, so the missing-ref branch is untested
